title: Serino 2015 peri-hand PPS Experiment 3
citation: Serino, A., Noel, J. P., Galli, G., Canzoneri, E., Marmaroli, P., Lissek, H., & Blanke, O. (2015). Body part-centered and full body-centered peripersonal space representations. Scientific Reports, 5, 18603.
notes: Peri-hand branch of the Serino body-part mapping series. The original two-speaker analog setup is treated as apparatus provenance and recreated as a binaural moving-sound trajectory. The lateralized hand posture is represented with an explicit cartesian hand-anchored path offset to shoulder width; exact hand side, original WAV/envelope files, and block/order rules remain caveats.

reference_parameters.analog_apparatus_recreation: Original near/far speakers are modeled as the reported moving-sound trajectory in the binaural renderer.

body_anchor_frame.hand_side: not reported; profile uses a right-side positive-x convention

remaining_caveats: exact original pink-noise WAV/noise seed is not reported
exact SoundForge envelope files are not provided beyond exponential direction and dB endpoints
exact hand side is not stated for Experiment 3
exact trial-order randomization, block count, and response timeout/window are not reported

provenance.source: Scientific Reports Experiment 3 reports five distances: 5, 27, 50, 71, and 93 cm.
Methods report 208 trials for Experiment 3 with 16 repetitions.

Manual review records that the hand was placed at shoulder width and the near/far speaker line was hand-relative. The profile encodes this with a positive-x cartesian offset and keeps the exact hand side as an unresolved caveat.
